title: Legacy map
description: Migration provenance, kept out of canonical identity: for every legacy suite, case and fixture, where it went in the canonical records, or why nothing carries it. Legacy names appear only on the `legacy` side of an entry (this is the provenance field); canonical ids on the other side are real records and are subject to the identity lint. It lets the compatibility exporter regenerate legacy names and lets a consumer trace every legacy fixture (ADR 0007). Lives under migration/ (one record per legacy suite once it is large: migration/legacy-map/<suite>.json). Added in schema revision 1.2.0.

id.description: The legacy name, verbatim. The one place a suite, beta or issue coordinate is allowed.

path.description: Where the legacy entity lived: a corpus path for a suite, the fixture's own path inside its corpus, the file the first import wrote for a case.

title.description: A suite's legacy title, verbatim (schema revision 1.3.0).

description.description: A suite's legacy description, verbatim (schema revision 1.3.0).

scenarioIds.description: The legacy navigation scenario ids the fixture carried in the legacy semantic index (schema revision 1.3.0). They are legacy data, not canonical Scenario ids; only the compatibility exporter reads them.

canonical.description: The canonical record that now carries it, several records when one legacy entity fans out (a suite, or a case that became a scenario and a plan cell; schema revision 1.3.0), or null when nothing does.

relation.description: same: carried one to one under a new semantic id. merged: several legacy entries fold into one canonical record. reclassified-as-scenario / reclassified-as-projection: the legacy case was a scenario instance or a matrix cell, not a reasoning unit. dropped: no canonical counterpart (canonical is null).
